ei.title: The Social Role of TV Sitcoms

fullPassage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more acceptable than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage acceptance of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.

questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social (A)[conflicts / harmonies] in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as (B)[evolving / fixed] conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more (C)[acceptable / unacceptable] than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage acceptance of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 갈등(conflicts), 진화하는(evolving), 수용 가능한(acceptable)이 문맥상 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① conflicts — evolving — acceptable: 사회적 '갈등', '진화하는' 가족 개념, 더 '수용 가능한' 가치.
❌ ② harmonies — evolving — acceptable: (A) 시트콤이 보여준 것은 사회적 '조화'가 아닌 '갈등'.
❌ ③ conflicts — fixed — acceptable: (B) 가족 개념은 '고정된' 것이 아니라 변화하는 것.
❌ ④ conflicts — evolving — unacceptable: (C) 유머를 통해 더 '수용 불가능한'이 아닌 '수용 가능한' 가치로 만듦.
det.tip: conflict(갈등) ↔ harmony(조화), evolve(진화하다) ↔ fix(고정하다)

questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been (A)[addressed / ignored] through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more acceptable than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, (B)[resisted / embraced] one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective (C)[means / barrier] to encourage acceptance of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 다루어졌다(addressed), 저항했다(resisted), 수단(means)이 문맥상 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ addressed — resisted — means: 각 쟁점이 유머를 통해 '다루어졌고', 편견적 인물이 발전에 '저항'했으며, 유머가 비용 효율적인 '수단'으로 기능.
❌ ① addressed — embraced — means: (B) 편견적 인물이 변화를 '수용'한 것이 아니라 '저항'함.
❌ ② ignored — resisted — means: (A) 쟁점을 '무시'한 것이 아니라 '다루었음'.
❌ ③ addressed — resisted — barrier: (C) 시트콤은 수용의 '장벽'이 아닌 '수단'으로 기능함.
det.tip: address(다루다) ↔ ignore(무시하다), resist(저항하다) ↔ embrace(수용하다), means(수단) ↔ barrier(장벽)

questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more (A)[progressive / conservative] values more acceptable than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear (B)[ridiculous / admirable]. They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage (C)[acceptance / rejection] of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 진보적인(progressive), 우스꽝스러운(ridiculous), 수용(acceptance)이 문맥상 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ progressive — ridiculous — acceptance: '진보적' 가치를 수용 가능하게 만들고, 편견적 인물을 '우스꽝스럽게' 보이게 하며, 다원적 사회의 '수용'을 장려.
❌ ① conservative — ridiculous — acceptance: (A) 시트콤은 '보수적' 가치가 아닌 '진보적' 가치를 확산.
❌ ② progressive — admirable — acceptance: (B) 편견적 인물이 '존경스럽게' 보이는 것은 문맥에 맞지 않음.
❌ ④ progressive — ridiculous — rejection: (C) 유머는 다원적 사회의 '거부'가 아닌 '수용'을 장려.
det.tip: progressive ↔ conservative, ridiculous ↔ admirable, acceptance ↔ rejection

questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been ①<u>addressed</u> through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more ②<u>acceptable</u> than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, ③<u>resisted</u> one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to ④<u>discourage</u> acceptance of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ discourage(막다)→encourage(장려하다). 시트콤의 유머는 다원적 사회의 수용을 '장려'하는 수단이었음.
det.analysis:
❌ ① addressed: '다루었다'는 문맥에 적절.
❌ ② acceptable: '수용 가능한'은 문맥에 적절.
❌ ③ resisted: '저항했다'는 편견적 인물의 행동으로 적절.
✅ inspire: encourage(장려하다)가 원문. inspire(막다)는 반의어로 문맥에 부적절.
det.tip: encourage(장려하다) ↔ discourage(막다, 단념시키다)

questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. Often a character, usually someone ①<u>marked</u> as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ②<u>admirable</u>. They were cut down either through their own ③<u>stupidity</u>, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage ④<u>acceptance</u> of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② admirable(존경할 만한)→ridiculous(우스꽝스러운). 편견적 인물은 '우스꽝스럽게' 보이도록 만들어짐.
det.analysis:
❌ ① marked: 편견이 심한 사람으로 '표시된'은 적절.
✅ ② admirable: ridiculous(우스꽝스러운)가 원문. admirable(존경할 만한)은 반의어로 부적절.
❌ ③ stupidity: 자신의 '어리석음'으로 조롱당한다는 문맥에 적절.
❌ ④ acceptance: '수용'을 장려한다는 문맥에 적절.
det.tip: ridiculous(우스꽝스러운) ↔ admirable(존경할 만한, 훌륭한)

questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as ①<u>evolving</u> conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more ②<u>progressive</u> values more acceptable than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a ③<u>costly</u> means to encourage acceptance of a more ④<u>pluralistic</u> and tolerant society.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ costly(비용이 많이 드는)→cost-effective(비용 효율적인). 시트콤의 유머는 비용 '효율적인' 수단이었지, '비용이 많이 드는' 수단이 아님.
det.analysis:
❌ ① evolving: 가족에 대한 '진화하는' 개념은 문맥에 적절.
❌ ② progressive: '진보적인' 가치는 문맥에 적절.
✅ ③ costly: cost-effective(비용 효율적인)가 원문. costly(비용이 많이 드는)는 반의적 의미로 부적절.
❌ ④ pluralistic: '다원적인' 사회는 문맥에 적절.
det.tip: cost-effective(비용 효율적인) ↔ costly(비용이 많이 드는)

questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more acceptable than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a __________, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage acceptance of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 편견이 심한 사람으로 묘사된 등장인물이 발전에 저항했다는 문맥에서 bigot(편견이 심한 사람)이 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① bigot: 편견이 심한 사람. 진보적 변화에 저항하는 인물의 특성으로 적절.
❌ ② hero: 영웅. 변화에 저항하고 우스꽝스럽게 보이는 인물을 영웅이라 칭하는 것은 부적절.
❌ ③ comedian: 코미디언. 시트콤 배역이지만 편견을 가진 인물을 가리키는 말로 부적절.
❌ ④ reformer: 개혁가. 변화에 저항하는 인물은 개혁가와 반대 성격.
det.tip: bigot = 편견이 심한 사람. 유의어: prejudiced person, narrow-minded person

questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving ____ of the family. Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more acceptable than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage acceptance of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 가족에 대한 진화하는 '개념'이라는 문맥에서 conceptions(개념)가 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② conceptions: 개념, 생각. 가족에 대해 변화하는 '개념'이라는 문맥에 적절.
❌ ① regulations: 규정. 가족에 대한 '규정'이 진화한다는 것은 부자연스러움.
❌ ③ restrictions: 제한. 가족에 대한 '제한'이 시트콤에서 다뤄졌다는 것은 부적절.
❌ ④ negotiations: 협상. 가족에 대한 '협상'은 문맥과 무관.
det.tip: conception = concept, idea, notion. '개념, 생각'이라는 뜻.

questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage acceptance of a more __________ and tolerant society.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 다원적이고 관용적인 사회의 수용을 장려한다는 문맥에서 pluralistic(다원적인)이 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ pluralistic: 다원적인. '관용적인(tolerant)'과 함께 다양성을 존중하는 사회를 나타내는 표현으로 적절.
❌ ① competitive: 경쟁적인. 관용적인 사회와 병렬되기에 맥락이 맞지 않음.
❌ ② authoritative: 권위적인. 유머로 장려하는 사회 성격과 상반됨.
❌ ③ homogeneous: 동질적인. 다문화주의를 다루는 시트콤이 '동질적인' 사회를 장려하는 것은 모순.
det.tip: pluralistic(다원적인) ↔ homogeneous(동질적인). plural(복수의) + -istic

questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social <u>conflicts</u> in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more acceptable than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage acceptance of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>conflicts</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: conflicts = 갈등, 충돌. disputes(분쟁)가 가장 가까운 의미입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ disputes: 분쟁, 갈등. conflict와 동의어.
❌ ① agreements: 합의. conflict의 반의어.
❌ ② celebrations: 축하. 완전히 다른 의미.
❌ ④ traditions: 전통. 관련 없는 의미.
det.tip: conflict = dispute, clash, disagreement ↔ harmony, agreement

questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been <u>addressed</u> through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more acceptable than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage acceptance of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>addressed</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: addressed = (문제를) 다루다, 처리하다. dealt with(다루다)가 가장 가까운 의미입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① dealt with: 다루다. address와 동의어로 '문제를 처리하다'의 의미.
❌ ② spoken to: ~에게 말하다. address의 다른 의미이지만 이 문맥에서는 부적절.
❌ ③ mailed to: ~에게 우편을 보내다. address의 다른 뜻에서 파생되지만 문맥과 무관.
❌ ④ pointed at: ~을 가리키다. address와는 다른 의미.
det.tip: address는 다의어: ① (문제를) 다루다 = deal with, handle, tackle ② (사람에게) 말하다 ③ 주소를 쓰다

questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more acceptable than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective <u>means</u> to encourage acceptance of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>means</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: means = 수단, 방법. method(방법)이 가장 가까운 의미입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② method: 방법, 수단. means와 동의어.
❌ ① wealth: 부, 재산. means의 다른 뜻(재력)이지만 이 문맥에서는 '수단'의 의미.
❌ ③ average: 평균. mean의 다른 뜻에서 파생되지만 문맥과 무관.
❌ ④ intention: 의도. '수단'과는 다른 개념.
det.tip: means는 다의어: ① 수단, 방법 = method, way ② 재력, 수입(복수형). by means of = ~을 통해

questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>progressive</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: progressive = 진보적인. conservative(보수적인)가 반의어입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ conservative: 보수적인. progressive(진보적인)의 정확한 반의어.
❌ ① aggressive: 공격적인. progressive와 어미(-ive)가 같지만 반의어 아님.
❌ ② excessive: 과도한. progressive와 무관.
❌ ③ impressive: 인상적인. 어미가 유사하지만 반의어 아님.
det.tip: progressive(진보적인) ↔ conservative(보수적인). 어미 -ive가 같은 단어로 혼동 유발 주의.

questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more acceptable than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage acceptance of a more pluralistic and <u>tolerant</u> society.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>tolerant</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: tolerant = 관대한, 아량 있는. intolerant(편협한)가 반의어입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ intolerant: 편협한. tolerant(관대한)의 정확한 반의어.
❌ ① tolerating: 참는(현재분사). tolerant의 동사형이지 반의어 아님.
❌ ② dominant: 지배적인. tolerant와 관련은 있으나 정확한 반의어 아님.
❌ ④ reluctant: 꺼리는. -ant 어미가 같지만 tolerant의 반의어 아님.
det.tip: tolerant(관대한) ↔ intolerant(편협한). open-minded ↔ narrow-minded

questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have <u>charted</u> many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more acceptable than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage acceptance of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 'charted'가 이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: charted = (과정을) 기록하다, 보여주다. 시트콤이 사회적 갈등의 변화를 '기록하다/추적하다'의 의미.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 기록하다, 추적하다: 시트콤이 미국 사회의 사회적 갈등을 시간에 따라 '기록하고 보여주었다'는 문맥.
❌ ① 도표로 만들다: chart의 사전적 의미 중 하나이지만, 시트콤이 갈등을 '도표로 만들었다'는 것은 부자연스러움.
❌ ③ 항로를 정하다: 항해 관련 의미로 이 문맥에 맞지 않음.
❌ ④ 순위를 매기다: 음악 차트 등에서 사용되는 의미로 이 문맥에 부적절.
det.tip: chart: ① (과정을) 기록하다, 보여주다 ② (항로를) 계획하다 ③ 도표/차트 ④ (순위에) 올리다

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a person who is intolerant of opinions, lifestyles, or identities differing from their own"

det.korean: 자신과 다른 의견, 생활 방식, 정체성에 편협한 사람 → bigot(편견이 심한 사람)
det.analysis:
✅ ① bigot: 편견이 심한 사람. 정의에 정확히 부합.
❌ ② critic: 비평가. 의견이 다른 사람에게 편협한 것과는 다른 개념.
❌ ③ skeptic: 회의론자. 의심이 많은 사람이지 편견과는 다름.
❌ ④ patriot: 애국자. 나라를 사랑하는 사람으로 편견과 무관.
det.tip: bigot = 편견이 심한 사람. bigotry = 편견, 불관용.

questions.passage: In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage __________ (accept) of a more pluralistic and tolerant society. Sitcoms used humour to promote diverse values.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: accept(동사) → acceptance(명사). encourage 뒤에 목적어가 필요하므로 명사형이 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ acceptance: 동사 accept의 명사형. encourage + 목적어(명사) 구조에 맞음.
❌ acceptable: 형용사형. 목적어 자리에 형용사는 부적절.
❌ accepted: 과거분사. 목적어 자리에 맞지 않음.
❌ accepting: 현재분사/동명사. 문맥상 acceptance가 더 자연스러움.
det.tip: accept(동사) → acceptance(명사) → acceptable(형용사). 명사형은 -ance 어미.

questions.passage: Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more __________ (progress) values more acceptable than previously. Humour served as a powerful tool for social change.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: progress(명사/동사) → progressive(형용사). values를 수식하는 형용사가 필요합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ progressive: progress의 형용사형. '진보적인 가치'라는 의미로 values를 수식.
❌ progression: 명사형. values 앞에 명사가 오면 의미가 부자연스러움.
❌ progressed: 과거분사. values를 수식하는 역할로 부적절.
❌ progressing: 현재분사. '진행 중인 가치'보다 '진보적인 가치'가 문맥에 적절.
det.tip: progress(명사/동사) → progressive(형용사) → progression(명사: 진행). -ive 어미는 형용사.

questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more acceptable than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. They were ____ either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage acceptance of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 편견적 인물이 자신의 어리석음이나 타인의 꾸지람으로 cut down(기세가 꺾이다)는 문맥입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ cut down: (기세를) 꺾다, 무안을 주다. 어리석음이나 꾸지람으로 체면을 잃는다는 문맥에 적절.
❌ ① lifted up: 들어 올리다. 조롱당하는 것과 반대 의미.
❌ ② backed up: 뒷받침하다. 편견적 인물이 지지받는 것은 문맥에 맞지 않음.
❌ ④ brought about: 초래하다. '인물이 초래되다'는 비문.
det.tip: cut down = (기세를) 꺾다, 무안을 주다. 유사: put down, humiliate

questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 시트콤의 유머가 다원적이고 관용적인 사회의 수용을 장려하는 cost-effective means(비용 효율적인 수단)로 작용했다는 문맥입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ cost-effective means: 비용 효율적인 수단. 시트콤이 유머를 통해 사회적 가치를 효과적으로 전달.
❌ ① mandatory requirement: 필수 요건. 시트콤의 유머가 '필수 요건'이라는 것은 문맥에 맞지 않음.
❌ ② significant obstacle: 중대한 장애물. 유머가 수용을 '장려'했으므로 장애물은 반대 의미.
❌ ③ temporary solution: 임시 해결책. 시트콤의 유머를 '임시적'으로 평가하는 내용은 원문에 없음.
det.tip: cost-effective = 비용 효율적인. means = 수단. cost-effective means = 비용 효율적인 수단
